q: Which Meta campaigns are wasting money?

checks.what: tool: uses spend plus an outcome metric

answer:
Short answer: Several Meta campaigns are spending substantial budget while returning less than ₹1 in gross sales per ₹1 spent (gross ROAS < 1). The biggest offenders (Oct 1–14, order-date basis for ROAS; ad spend on delivery date) are:

- TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ — Ad spend ₹55,793 · Gross ROAS 0.9 (₹0.94 per ₹1)  
- TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP — Ad spend ₹49,163 · Gross ROAS 0.9 (₹0.92 per ₹1)  
- CAT TOY CS-26SEP — Ad spend ₹28,431 · Gross ROAS 0.9 (₹0.93 per ₹1)  
- DOG TOY CS-24SEP — Ad spend ₹19,622 · Gross ROAS 1.0 (₹0.97 per ₹1)  
- TH-348-FUSIONHARNESS-03OCT — Ad spend ₹14,667 · Gross ROAS 0.7 (₹0.75 per ₹1)  
- DOG DAD T-SHIRT-CS-06OCT — Ad spend ₹14,069 · Gross ROAS 1.0 (₹0.96 per ₹1)

Why this matters (top drivers):
- Spend concentrated on a few product campaigns with ROAS below 1 — each rupee spent returns less than a rupee of gross sales, so these campaigns reduce contribution margin.
- Some campaigns show near-zero or zero ROAS (no attributed order revenue) — any non-trivial spend on those is pure waste until creative/targeting or attribution is fixed.
- Totals and ROAS are order-date (gross ROAS from the P&L/order view) while ad spend is platform delivery date (standard mismatch; figures above are the platform spend vs order-date gross ROAS slice for Meta).

Worth checking: pause or reduce budget on the top 3 listed and reallocate to higher-ROAS campaigns; investigate the zero-ROAS campaigns for tracking/attribution or poor targeting before more spend.
